findings.title: bind_account proof is a static, replayable message
findings.impact: One captured signature grants a permanent Prism session for the victim: reads /v1/me, /v1/me/balance, /v1/activity, /v1/claims, resolves aliases as them, and flips privacy/profile settings (which require no account signature). Not fund theft.
findings.fix: server-issued single-use challenge with TTL, chainId and expiry in the signed payload; extend account-signature enforcement to setPrivacy/setProfile
findings.notFixedBecause: the payload is co-defined in ios/MeraBridge/MeraAccountManager.swift and the iOS half cannot be compiled or tested here

findings.title: A lost relayer response caused a blind re-broadcast (MUT-16)
findings.impact: A retry after a lost response re-entered the relayer and re-broadcast the same authorization. On-chain guards prevented a double-spend, but it burned relayer gas; fundClaim additionally marked a claim failed while its funding may have been landing.
findings.fix: operations move to a 'broadcasting' state before the relay call; errors are classified pre-broadcast vs ambiguous; an ambiguous retry reads AUSD.authorizationState(payer, nonce) and resolves to 'confirming' instead of resending
findings.regressionTests: backend/test/mutation-audit.test.js MUT-16 x3; verified to fail against the pre-fix code

findings.title: Alias-lookup rate limit is per-identity with no global or per-IP cap
findings.impact: 60 lookups/hour per Prism identity; an attacker minting N identities gets 60N. Identity creation costs an OTP plus an account-control signature, which raises but does not bound the cost.

findings.title: Identity-change trust store lives in UserDefaults, not the Keychain
findings.impact: TOFU pins in ios/Prism/Features/People/PeopleView.swift are readable and writable from an unencrypted device backup, so the MUT-14 identity-change warning can be suppressed.

findings.title: Claim authorizer key is a single point of failure
findings.impact: PrismClaimVault.claim releases funds on one authorizer signature plus the recipient's intent; the intent proves who is asking, not who is entitled. aliasVersion is signed but never compared to on-chain state. Compromise drains every funded claim. KMS/HSM is load-bearing.

findings.title: Resolver pepper is stored beside the data it protects
findings.impact: phoneIndex is HMAC-SHA256(pepper, E164) over a ~10^10 space with a fast primitive; an attacker taking both the datastore and RESOLVER_PEPPER can enumerate every user's number offline.

findings.title: The iOS app did not compile
findings.impact: Five Swift 6 strict-concurrency errors under SWIFT_VERSION 6.0 in PrismHaptics.swift, PaymentCoordinator.swift and OnboardingFlow.swift. The Face ID gate and the MUT-15 `.sent` binding reviewed by this audit were in files that did not build.
findings.detectedBy: CI macos-15 job, after the audit branch was pushed — not reproducible locally (Linux)
findings.fix: @MainActor on PrismHaptics (UIKit feedback generators are main-actor isolated); BiometricService.authenticate returns Void instead of the non-Sendable LAContext, which neither caller used

findings.title: Onboarding failed in CI: Keychain writes rejected because the build had no entitlements
findings.impact: Alert "Prism.KeychainError error 0" after account creation. CI built with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="", so the app had no application-identifier and every SecItemAdd failed with errSecMissingEntitlement. Onboarding stores the PIN and the dev signer seed in the Keychain.
findings.next: the UI test now captures alert title, body and visible static text on every bail-out; the next run should name the cause
findings.note: left failing deliberately — a red CI job reflecting a real bug is the correct state for this branch
findings.rootCause: CI configuration artifact, not a product defect — a signed build (any device build) is unaffected.
findings.fix: drop the signing overrides so the simulator default ad-hoc identity applies entitlements; keep CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO
findings.secondary: KeychainStore collapses every SecItemAdd failure into KeychainError.write and discards the OSStatus, which is why the alert named nothing useful
